article.title: Why Writing Down an Assumption Can Prevent Rework
article.why: Make important assumptions visible before work begins so misunderstandings are corrected early.
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

sources.label: Background: project communication and requirements practice

paragraphs.en:
Starting a task quickly can feel productive, but speed is wasted when the task begins with the wrong assumption. An assumption is something we believe to be true before we have fully checked it. In everyday work, assumptions are often about the target customer, the data period, the meaning of a metric, the owner of a task, or the expected output.

Imagine that a manager asks you to compare sales with last year. You may assume that “last year” means the same calendar months. The manager may actually mean the previous fiscal year. If you build the whole analysis first, the mistake may be discovered only during review. Then you have to change the data, charts, and explanation.

A simple habit can prevent this kind of rework: write down the important assumption before you start. For example, you can say, “I will compare June 2026–May 2027 with June 2025–May 2026.” This short sentence gives the other person a chance to correct you early.

Not every detail needs confirmation. The goal is not to ask a question about everything. Focus on assumptions that could change the result, require significant rework, or affect another person’s decision.

This habit is especially useful when instructions are short or ambiguous. A written assumption makes your interpretation visible. It also creates a small record that the team can return to later. In a meeting, you can confirm it in one sentence. In chat, you can put it before the task update. The method is simple, but it changes hidden interpretation into something the team can inspect.

Good work is not only about completing tasks quickly. It is also about reducing avoidable loops. A one-minute assumption check at the beginning can save an hour of correction at the end.
paragraphs.zh: 快速開始工作看起來很有效率，但如果一開始的前提就錯了，速度反而會變成浪費。假設通常涉及目標客群、資料期間、指標定義、負責人或預期輸出。與其等到 review 才發現理解不同，不如在開始前把關鍵假設寫成一句話，例如明確寫出比較期間。並不是所有細節都要逐一確認，而是優先確認那些一旦錯誤就會改變結果、造成大量返工或影響他人決策的前提。把假設寫下來，可以把原本藏在腦中的理解變成團隊可檢查的資訊。
paragraphs.ja: 仕事を早く始めても、前提が間違っていれば手戻りが増えます。対象顧客、データ期間、指標の定義、担当者、成果物など、結果を大きく左右する前提は着手前に一文で明示すると効果的です。すべてを確認する必要はなく、間違えた場合に大きな修正が必要になる前提を優先します。前提を書き出すことで、自分の頭の中だけにあった解釈を相手が確認できる状態にできます。

vocabulary.usage: Write down the key assumption before you start.
An early check can prevent rework.
Clarify assumptions when instructions are ambiguous.
Confirm assumptions that could change the result.

phrases.term: Before I start, I’m assuming that…
phrases.explanation: 開始工作前柔和地明示自己的前提。
phrases.example: Before I start, I’m assuming that the analysis covers the fiscal year.

grammar.title: If + present, can + verb
grammar.body: 用來說明某個條件可能造成的結果，例如：If we confirm the period now, we can avoid rework later.

business.term: Let me confirm one assumption before I proceed.
business.explanation: 在著手前只確認一個關鍵前提，語氣自然且不顯得過度確認。
business.example: Let me confirm one assumption before I proceed: the target is active customers only, correct?

business.explanation: 把自己的理解明示出來，方便對方直接修正。
business.example: My current understanding is that we should compare the same fiscal-year periods.

quiz.question: Which assumptions should you confirm first?
quiz.answer: Assumptions that could change the result, cause significant rework, or affect another person’s decision.
